figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The subtitle's '140 GB: NVLink 544 ms | HDR 6,125 ms | RoCE 98,000 ms' is ambiguous about what the 140 GB denotes. The x-axis is 'Logical input tensor per rank (GB)', while the plotted time uses 1.75× that value as sent bytes per rank. A reader can misread 140 GB as the sent-bytes-per-rank value, which would make the plotted times inconsistent with the subtitle.
evidence: The subtitle says 'sent bytes per rank = 1.75 × tensor bytes' and then '140 GB: NVLink 544 ms...'. The caption clarifies 'Each rank sends 1.75 times the logical tensor size', but the subtitle alone does not. At x=140 GB logical tensor, sent bytes per rank = 245 GB; 245/450 = 0.544 s, 245/40 = 6.125 s, 245/2.5 = 98 s. The numbers are correct only under the logical-tensor reading.
acceptance_test: Revise the subtitle to say '140 GB logical tensor per rank (245 GB sent/rank): NVLink 544 ms | HDR 6,125 ms | RoCE 98,000 ms' or equivalent, so the 140 GB quantity is explicitly tied to the x-axis and the 1.75× multiplier is visible at the point of use.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The dashed red setup arrows run from the launcher/rendezvous box directly to the NCCL and oneCCL boxes, bypassing the ProcessGroupNCCL and ProcessGroupXCCL framework-backend boxes. This visually implies that the framework backend is not involved in communicator setup, which is misleading: in common stacks the framework backend is the component that creates the communicator and passes the rendezvous/unique-ID information into the collective library.
evidence: The diagram's top box says 'Launcher, rank/device mapping, rendezvous' and 'MPI or a store can distribute communicator IDs.' The dashed red arrows go from that box down the outside to the '2 Collective library and algorithm' row (NCCL/oneCCL). The '1 Framework backend' row (ProcessGroupNCCL/ProcessGroupXCCL) has only solid payload arrows down to the collective library. The caption says 'Payload layers and communicator setup are different paths', but the setup path as drawn skips the framework backend entirely. The prose on printed p. 152 says 'The framework chooses a communication group and operation; its backend connects that request to a collective implementation', which describes the payload path but does not justify removing the backend from setup.
acceptance_test: Either (a) route the dashed setup path through the framework-backend boxes (launcher/rendezvous → ProcessGroupNCCL/XCCL → NCCL/oneCCL), or (b) add an explicit note in the figure or caption that the dashed path represents only the bootstrap/unique-ID distribution and that the framework backend still participates in communicator creation. The revised figure must not allow the inference that ProcessGroupNCCL/XCCL is absent from setup.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The legend label 'Payload / device execution' is too broad for the solid arrows. The upper solid arrows (framework backend → collective library) represent API/control calls, not device execution. A reader can infer that all solid arrows are device execution, which is not true.
evidence: The solid arrows from '1 Framework backend' (ProcessGroupNCCL/XCCL) to '2 Collective library and algorithm' (NCCL/oneCCL) are software API calls. Only the lower solid arrows (collective library → device runtime → physical resources) involve device execution. The legend uses one label for both.
acceptance_test: Change the legend to distinguish 'Payload path (API + device execution)' from 'Control/setup', or use two solid-arrow styles: one for API/control submission and one for device execution. The revised legend must not equate the framework-backend-to-collective-library call with device execution.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The right-hand '3 Device runtime plus transport' box labels 'MPI or OFI' as 'Legacy plugin'. The prose on printed p. 152 describes oneCCL's transport layer as including MPI and OFI paths without calling either 'legacy'. The word 'Legacy' is an unsupported value judgment in the figure and may become stale or misleading.
evidence: Printed p. 152: 'oneCCL's transport layer includes MPI as well as OFI paths (oneCCL MPI transport, pinned; oneCCL OFI transport, pinned).' Figure 9.3 right box: 'Legacy plugin: MPI or OFI'. The caption dates the snapshot to 2026-10-28 but does not justify the 'Legacy' label.
acceptance_test: Remove 'Legacy' or replace it with a neutral, dated descriptor such as 'Plugin path: MPI or OFI (2026-10-28 snapshot)'. The figure must not imply that MPI/OFI is deprecated unless the prose and a primary source support that claim.
